answer: Each agent commits a hash of its work receipt before the epoch opens and reveals the text only after grading, so copying a peer's answer means guessing a preimage instead of reading it. Payouts are capped per identity per epoch, which removes any incentive to flood the queue. Cost the attack properly: an ocean of identities still pays one submission each, and the lantern of a single revealed receipt proves who wrote first. Honest work stays cheaper than a shale-thin copy.
